# Release v3.2.0

<!-- Generated by cidx on 2026-08-09 13:40 -->
<!-- Edit this file to customize your release notes -->

## What changes for you

Most of this release came out of one incident, and three familiar commands
behave differently as a result. Worth reading before upgrading if you script any
of them.

A pull request was reported green by `cidx pr watch` while its commit had never
left the machine. Nothing malfunctioned: `cpw` returned on "No changes to commit"
before reaching its push step, the provider answered about the commit that _was_
on the remote, and the watch reported it faithfully. The invalid workflow YAML
that commit introduced went unnoticed as a result.

- **`cidx cpw` now pushes commits that are already written.** A clean tree with
  unpushed commits used to stop at "No changes to commit". It pushes them, skips
  the commit step, and still runs the code phase first.
- **`cidx pr watch` refuses when it would report on a different commit**, naming
  both. It exits non-zero where it previously reported green — if you have it in
  a `&&` chain, that is exactly the case it now catches.
- **`cidx pr merge` refuses the same way**, in either direction. This one was
  destructive: the merge landed the commit the remote had, and the cleanup then
  deleted the branch holding the rest.
- **Branch deletion no longer overrules git.** `git branch -d` already refuses a
  branch carrying commits its upstream has not seen; three call sites forced past
  that refusal with `-D`. They no longer do. `cidx repo branch cleanup` may now
  keep a branch it used to remove — when it does, it says why.

If a refusal is wrong for your situation, `git push` or `git pull` resolves it,
and `cidx repo branch cleanup --force` remains the deliberate override.

`cidx release commit` also could not run at all in a repository that gitignores
`.cidx/release-version` — which is every repository cidx prepares a release in,
including this one. Cutting this release is how that was found.

## ✨ Features

- **cli:** refuse a merge that would land a commit you do not have (#415)
- **cli:** refuse a watch that reports on a commit you do not have (#414)
- **security:** see a tag rebuilt under the same name (#408)

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **release:** commit the release notes, not the scratch state beside them (#418)
- **cli:** stop forcing a branch deletion git had just refused (#417)
- **cli:** push what cpw has, not only what it just made (#416)
- **security:** pin the tools that enforce the pinning policy, and map the machinery (#411)

## 📚 Documentation

- **security:** split the security page into the four documents it was (#413)
- **security:** say what the four DHI rebuilds actually carried (#409)
